stories.headline: Iranian attacks sink container ships in the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran vows to keep fighting

sources.body:
Vessels were hit by missiles as rise in strikes suggests Iran is trying to close waterway before US midterm elections

Two container ships near the strait of Hormuz have ⁠sunk after being struck by missiles, amid the sharpest rise in Iranian attacks on shipping since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran .

The increase in attacks suggests Iran is trying to fully close the strategic waterway in an attempt to frustrate Donald Trump’s efforts to bring down fuel prices before the US midterm elections on 3 November.

The Trump administration has been attempting to deflect attention from the economic impact of the war on Iran by blaming Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries for increased fuel prices.

On Wednesday, UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported at least five incidents including drone strikes in the previous 48 hours targeting tankers and other commercial ships around the Hormuz area.

“There is a tempo increase in strikes, which looks deliberate,” one maritime security source said.

The Singapore-flagged ​container ‌ship GFS Pride sank on Wednesday after an attack the previous day. Hours later, the Antigua- and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao sank close to the strait, having been hit by a ​projectile ​on 23 September, according to data from ‌the ‌International Maritime Organization.

Apparently referring to the GFS Pride, Iran said a cargo ship had sunk after hitting a naval mine while making an unauthorised passage through the strait.

State television quoted a statement from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that said the ship was travelling on an “illegal and dangerous route” when it hit the mine.

The ship, which was shown tilted in the water and spewing a thick plume of smoke, was carrying 2,500 containers, the broadcast said.

However, UKMTO suggested that both ships had been hit by unidentified projectiles, raising questions over Tehran’s account.

Iran has repeatedly warned ships against trying to transit through the strait without its approval. The US military has been guiding ships through the waterway on a route nearer to Oman’s coast.

Ships in the area were reporting an intense series of attacks in recent days, with six vessels attacked on Sunday alone, according to UKMTO’s monitoring.

Analysis by the Financial Times said 24 ships were hit in the two weeks to 11 October. Of the vessels hit, three were refined energy product tankers and two others were crude oil tankers.

The increased tempo of Iranian attacks appears to have caused a dramatic drop-off in oil shipments through the strait, as Tehran appears determined to demonstrate its ability to strike ships before the US midterms that will decide control of Congress.

US fuel prices have surged by almost 70% since Trump launched his war on Iran, and the Republican party is bracing for punishment at the polls.

According to two Iranian officials, Iran has recently begun using new tactics against vessels it considers to be in violation of its restrictions. The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being ⁠to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said.
sources.headline: Two container ships sink near strait of Hormuz amid surge in Iranian attacks

sources.body: Oil prices gain as Houthi strikes hit Saudi Aramco and Tehran vows new tactics against shipping in Hormuz.
sources.headline: Iran vows to fight until US accepts demands; ships sink in Hormuz

stories.headline: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions are crippling drone and air-defence operations

sources.body:
Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.

An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

Musk said that Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government, and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]".

Musk - writing on X - had been responding to pleas from Ukrainian officials to restore connectivity, including from Zelensky who told UK media: "I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem. I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on."

Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.

It had been partially restored by Wednesday evening, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.

"Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," he wrote on X, thanking Elon Musk and asking for his "continued support".

About an hour later, Musk replied to that post, defending his company's involvement.

"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," he wrote.

Musk added that Starlink is for "civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company".

In the early hours of Thursday, Russian strikes killed two people in the Dnipropetrovsk region, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.

While both companies are owned by Musk's SpaceX, Starlink is a civilian service that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas, while Starshield is designed for government and military use.

The restrictions on Tuesday night came as Russia launched deadly attacks against Ukraine that killed several people in Kyiv, officials said, and hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Zelensky said it was "one of the largest attacks" from Russia, and while "a significant part of the drones were shot down" there were "also hits".

At least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity, and residents said they received no warning of incoming drones before they hit.

"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram on Wednesday morning.

US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated towards Ukraine as it continues to strike Russian energy facilities.
sources.headline: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sources.body: Elon Musk’s ⁠SpaceX restricted “military-grade” ​Starlink services overnight into Wednesday, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses, Ukraine reported. In response, Musk said that the US government was behind any slowdown in Ukraine's Starshield system.
sources.headline: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?

stories.headline: Indonesia battles toxic haze as El Niño-fuelled fires spread

sources.body:
Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South Sumatra

As fires ravage Indonesia , emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice.

Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fires, Indonesia’s coordinating security minister said dry ice would be dropped on the province of South Sumatra on Thursday.

“This trial of dry ice dispersal is being conducted under the president’s direct instruction to help tackle the haze in South Sumatra,” minister Dudung Abdurachman, was quoted as saying by state news agency Antara.

“We will first observe the results, and if effective, there is a possibility that this method could be implemented in other regions.”

Since January, almost 900,000 hectares have been burned Indonesia-wide in the worst fire season in more than a decade, exacerbated by this year’s “godzilla” El-Nino and as the practice of “slash and burn” to clear land for crops such as palm oil persists.

For months, millions of Indonesians have been subject to thick smoke and an apocalyptic tangerine haze, with criticism mounting of the government’s response, including a class action lawsuit filed last week accusing it of “gross negligence”. Tens of thousands of people have sought treatment for respiratory illness linked to the haze.

Air quality has also plummeted in neighbouring countries, shuttering schools, grounding flights and driving a spike in respiratory illness.

The haze has drifted into neighbouring Singapore , Malaysia and as far afield as the Philippines. Timor-Leste has said it would shut schools nationwide for three days from Thursday and urged families to keep children indoors or to use “respiratory protection” if going outside.

Singapore rolled out subsidies for haze-related medical treatment starting on Monday, a measure last activated in 2015 when similar blazes occurred. The city-state has also begun distributing N95 masks to eligible residents.

In the past week, the financial hub of Singapore was listed among the most polluted cities globally. Kuala Lumpur, also deeply affected, was at number two.

On Thursday, a Cessna aircraft will reportedly disperse 1.5 tons of dry ice over the South Sumatran city of Palembang, a move the government hopes will ease the smoke and improve air quality and visibility.

The technique was first deployed in the 1940s to promote ice formation in clouds, Bloomberg reported.

But experts say the use of dry ice, or solid carbon dioxide, might only offer local, and limited relief.

“It’s got some potential for local relief that might work for a while,” says Rick McRae, an adjunct professor from the University of New South Wales’ (UNSW) bushfire research group.

“Weather systems are all moving from east to west. So if you’re in a town under that and you clear the smoke, there’s gonna be more blowing all the time,” he says, “So it’s a constant … It’s not going to be simple and it’s not going to be a permanent fix in any way.”
sources.headline: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region

sources.body:
A thick orange smog has descended on the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya.

Witnesses captured videos of the haze washing over the Kalimantan region not far from where wildfires continue to burn.

The ISPU air pollution index exceeded 1,200, according to data from the national environment ministry, four times higher than the "hazardous" level of 300 on Wednesday.

Toxic smog is choking millions across Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia, with authorities partly blaming the agricultural clearing method known as "slash and burn" for compounding the intense haze.

Châtaigniers en fleurs, also known as Chestnut Trees in Blossom, is expected to receive record bids at auction this weekend.

A flash flood at the Budhi Gandaki River has swept away several buildings and bridges, two months after catastrophic floods hit the country.

Tens of thousands of security personnel have been deployed and roads barricaded in Delhi to stop the latest Cockroach Janta Party demonstration.

Thailand’s Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The municipality building in Baglung was left teetering on an unstable ledge due to floods before it fell into a river.

As sellers waded through floodwaters to sell produce like fish and vegetables from floating platforms and foam boxes, buyers walked or paddled between the makeshift stalls to buy their groceries.

BBC correspondent Azadeh Moshiri reports from Delhi, where hundreds of women are protesting.

Heavy rain over the last two days has overwhelmed Bangkok's water systems, with more rain forecast on Sunday.

Days of near continuous downpours have caused widespread flooding in the Thai capital.

The BBC is in Inner Mongolia where dozen of Chinese data centres are being constructed, as the country aims to lead the world in artificial intelligence.

Lian Yunzhi broke the women's world record twice in three days at World Cube Association competitions.

The typhoon is passing Japan's eastern coast, bringing major disruption and heavy rainfall in its wake.

Verified footage appears to show a cargo ship colliding with a fishing boat near Singapore, with investigators still working to establish exactly when and how the crash happened.

The BBC goes inside a fortified storage facility to view luxury goods seized by police that are now up for auction.

Rescuers are searching for survivors after the vessel travelling from the mainland to a popular tourist destination caught fire.

Emergency teams were still searching for at least 86 missing people in the waters off the coast of Coron, in the Philippines.

Police say they hope the drill will help prepare students, as concern grows over the increase in school shootings in South East Asia.

Chandika Shrestha was airlifted to hospital after spending more than 10 days in her partially buried house.

There are still hundreds of workers trapped in a network of tunnels that run along the Trishuli river.

Rescuers pull two people from a hydropower tunnel more than a week after a massive flash flood devastated the Nepal-China border.
sources.headline: 'Nowhere to escape' - Indonesians share footage of orange haze blanketing towns

stories.headline: Protests in Albania turn violent for a second night as demonstrators demand the prime minister resign

sources.body:
Dozens of people detained after government building and two banks set on fire as tens of thousands march over education costs and corruption

Tens of thousands of students have taken to the streets of Tirana, the Albanian capital, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and ⁠corruption.

Police responded with water ⁠cannon and teargas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned bins and smashed the fronts of local businesses. A branch of Raiffeisen Bank near the education ministry also caught fire.

Authorities said 23 police officers and six other people were being treated for injuries and that 35 people had been detained.

President Bajram Begaj condemned the violence and appealed for calm, adding: “The constitution and the law must remain the boundaries for everyone, without exception.”

The protests are the most violent outburst yet against Edi Rama, ⁠the prime minister, who won a fourth term in office in May last year but has since faced ​growing discontent at perceived graft surrounding top ‌officials. Protesters also dismiss opposition figures ‌as unpalatable alternatives.

The unrest caps a summer of peaceful protests against Rama, triggered by the proposed development ‌of a luxury resort along Albania’s pristine southern coast backed by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, which has been caught up in legal disputes.

“This is a revolution. We are tired of peaceful protests. We will not stop until Rama resigns,” said Lora, a student who declined to give her last name as she threw rocks at the police.

Others chanted “resignation” and “police of crime”.

Student ‌organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, a lack of financial support and employment prospects after graduation.

The unrest is part of a ​broader wave of student activism sweeping Europe over education and living conditions. In France, high school students have staged weeks of protests and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.

Albanian media reported that Wednesday’s protests had spread to universities at Elbasan and Shkodër.

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

Albana Koçiu, the deputy prime minister of Albania, said on Facebook: “Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used ​as an excuse for violence, city ​destruction or ugly fighting in the middle ​of the road. I call on ​students and every ‌honest citizen who believes in ​the right to ​protest: distance yourself from violence and vandalism!”

The police issued a statement calling for calm. “Any person who uses violence, burns or destroys property, or attacks police officers, bears individual responsibility and will face the law, in accordance with the offences committed,” they said.
sources.headline: Student protests in Albania turn violent as demonstrators clash with police

sources.body: Anti-government protests in Albania’s capital Tirana turned violent for a second consecutive night on Wednesday, leaving several government buildings damaged and at least one ablaze. Thousands demanded Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation and improved university conditions. Police fired tear gas and deployed water cannons as protesters smashed windows and attacked buildings.
sources.headline: Albania protests turn violent as protestors demand PM Rama's resignation

stories.headline: North Korea test-fires submarine-launched cruise missiles amid rising tensions

sources.body:
The tests showcase North Korea’s war deterrent capabilities in the region, KCNA says.

North Korea has test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in the sea off its east coast, state media KCNA reports.

The test-fire on Wednesday aimed to examine the reliability of war deterrents and improve the navy’s skill in performing strategic missions, the outlet said.

One of the missiles fired was a Pulhwasal-3-31, the same type of strategic cruise missile North Korea said it test-fired from land last week, according to KCNA.

Senior military officers observed the tests conducted at sea off the country’s east coast. KCNA added that the tests had no adverse impact on the security of neighbouring countries.

North Korea is not yet believed to have launched a modern missile submarine in full operation. This is a top military priority of the country’s leader Kim Jong Un, who has overseen the development of a range of strategic ballistic and cruise missiles.

Last year, Kim Jong Un criticised a nuclear submarine deal between the US and South Korea while he toured his country’s submarine production facility, where state media images showed an 8,700-tonne nuclear-powered missile submarine under construction. On his tour, he described the deal as a threat to the stability of the Korean Peninsula, KCNA reported.

Pyongyang has fired off a flurry of missiles in recent weeks.

Earlier this week, North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea off its east coast, adding to a series of tests as tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang are on the rise.

On October 3, North Korea also tested a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to evade missile defences in South Korea and Japan.

After the ballistic missile launch, Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said the move appeared to be a show of force as it came days after South Korea tested its own hypersonic weapon.

Last week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country’s first test firing of a hypersonic missile, a rare public showcase of a missile test by a South Korean president.

Lee’s office said the hypersonic weapon, once fully developed, would enhance South Korea’s ability to strike key targets by surprise in the “Korean Peninsula theatre of operations”.

Inter-Korean relations have further soured as a landmine blast , which Seoul blamed on North Korea, wounded three soldiers in September in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) between the two countries.

A joint South Korean-United Nations investigation concluded that two landmines that exploded last month in the DMZ were planted by North Korean forces about a year ago, prompting Seoul to demand an official apology.

Pyongyang has sharply accelerated military fortification along the DMZ as part of leader Kim Jong Un’s “hostile-states” policy, launched in 2023, to permanently sever ties with South Korea.

Diplomatic efforts on the Korean Peninsula have stalled since the collapse of denuclearisation talks between Washington and Pyongyang in 2019 during the first Trump administration. While Trump has floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in his second term, no such meeting has materialised.
sources.headline: North Korea tests two submarine-launched missiles, state media reports

sources.body: North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported Thursday, saying the launches posed no threat to neighbouring countries. The tests follow heightened tensions with South Korea after a September 21 landmine explosion in the Demilitarised Zone injured three South Korean soldiers.
sources.headline: North Korea test-fires submarine-launched cruise missiles amid rising tensions

stories.headline: Kenya confirms a second Ebola case

sources.body:
Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola, 10 days after a businessman died of the virus after he had travelled to the East African nation from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The new patient, a 39-year-old man, is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill on Tuesday, Kenya's health ministry says.

The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.

Detecting his illness early had improved his chances of recovery and limited the chance of him passing the virus on to others, the ministry said, as it urged the public to "stay calm but vigilant".

"Both cases are linked, and there is no evidence of spread in the wider community," the ministry said.

"Kenya remains open, with no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings", it added.

The 40-year-old Kenyan man who died on 5 October was diagnosed with Ebola shortly after being admitted to hospital in the capital, Nairobi.

A relative had taken him there shortly after picking him up at the airport. He had travelled from DR Congo, through Uganda to Kenya without his illness being detected.

Since his death, officials had determined that he had been in contact with 128 people - and since Tuesday 113 of them had been found, the health ministry said.

Of these, 108 were in quarantine in Kenya and tracing of the remaining 15 continued, it said.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

"Anyone with fever, unusual tiredness, muscle or joint pains, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding should seek care promptly at the nearest health facility," Kenya's health ministry said.

The current outbreak in DR Congo, which began in May, has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died.

However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the continent's leading public health agency, has reconstructed the Kenyan patient's movements for the six weeks leading up to his death.

It revealed that he first started feeling unwell in DR Congo on 15 September - and showed how several opportunities to detect the infection were missed, including during several visits to Congolese medical facilities.

He then managed to travel through Uganda to Kenya - and was again not detected at airports screenings.

Health experts say it highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations.

Go to BBCAfrica.com for more news from the African continent.

Follow us on Twitter @BBCAfrica , on Facebook at BBC Africa or on Instagram at bbcafrica
sources.headline: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim

sources.body: In tonight's edition, Kenya confirms a second case of Ebola. Also, Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay warns that international justice is facing growing pressure. And millions of people in Nigeria have been without Tiktok for about a month.
sources.headline: Kenya reports second Ebola case

stories.headline: Brazil cuts its work week to 40 hours ahead of the presidential runoff

sources.body:
Congress approves constitutional amendment that bans six-day workweeks, which could effect up to 30 million

Brazil’s congress has approved a constitutional amendment to shorten the working week to a maximum of 40 hours, a move that could affect 30 million workers and that will hand a political victory to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of the presidential runoff in under two weeks.

In an attempt to overturn the first-round lead secured by his opponent, far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which will give some workers an extra day off each week.

Bolsonaro, by contrast, spent months opposing the change but reversed course on Tuesday, saying “the majority of Brazilian workers” supported it. On Wednesday, he joined 75 senators who approved the reform, which passed the lower house in May.

Only one senator voted against it: Hamilton Mourão, former vice-president to Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio’s father.

The constitutional amendment bans six-day workweeks, currently worked by 16 million people, while cutting the maximum workweek from 44 to 40 hours for more than 30 million workers.

The change is expected to affect mainly workers in retail, restaurants and hotels, most of them low-paid – one of the groups which Lula lost the most support from since the 2022 election, when he defeated Jair Bolsonaro.

Lula celebrated the amendment’s passing, writing on social media “ending the 6x1 schedule is about more than changing working hours. It means more time to live, rest, be with family, watch your children grow up, look after yourself and enjoy life.”

Victor Escobar, a researcher at the Laboratory of Parties, Elections and Comparative Politics, said the change “could indeed benefit Lula’s re-election campaign”.

The proposal began as a TikTok movement called Life Beyond Work, founded by a pharmacy assistant who entered politics after its success and later was embraced by Lula.

His party spent months pushing the senate to put the proposal to a vote and many believed that after the far right’s sweeping victory last week secured a broad congressional majority in 2027, the Senate would no longer vote on it.

But Senate president Davi Alcolumbre, whose relationship with Lula has at times been rocky, put it to a vote.

Flávio Bolsonaro’s party had considered blocking it, but polls showed the change had more than 70% of the general population behind it, and more than half of the senator’s voters.

In May, Bolsonaro said the proposal could cause “mass unemployment”, an argument employers’ associations opposed to the change have repeatedly made.

The senator voted remotely while campaigning in the country’s south.

Even after changing his position, Bolsonaro said on Tuesday that he “supports something even better,” referring to an alternative proposal he had long advocated in which pay would be based on the hours actually worked. The Folha newspaper reported that he told business leaders that, if elected, he would review parts of the new amendment, a point several allied senators also made during Wednesday’s vote.
sources.headline: Brazil cuts work week to 40 hours in win for Lula ahead of runoff

stories.headline: US inflation rises more than expected, intensifying concerns before the midterms

sources.body:
US inflation rose by more than expected in the year to September, according to official figures, in the final data release before the midterm elections next month.

The pace of price rises increased to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in the 12 months to August.

Inflation was above forecasts, driven by higher petrol prices, which have risen following disruption to Middle East energy supplies due to the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

The elections are being fought over cost-of-living pressures across the US.

Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increases over time.

For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%.

Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI).

It tracks the price changes of hundreds of day-to-day items including fresh food, gasoline and medical services to work out the overall level of inflation in the US economy.

The bureau updates this so-called basket of goods over time as peoples' spending and lifestyle habits change.

There are several factors that can cause inflation to rise.

If demand for a product outstrips its supply, that can lead to producers raising prices - the craze for Labubu dolls in recent years and the high resale prices are an example.

Higher incomes can also lead to higher demand, for example, which in turn pushes up prices.

Supply can also affect inflation. If supply of a product is reduced, but demand remains constant, that can cause prices to rise. A good example of this is crude oil, which is used to make gasoline and diesel.

Before the US-Israel war with Iran began, it was trading at just over $70 a barrel, but when the conflict constricted crude supplies, the price quickly rose and is currently over $100.

Inflation has risen to 3.7% in the year to September, which is a higher-than-expected increase fuelled by petrol prices.

Vehicle fuel prices jumped by 34.2% over 12 months.

In September alone, they jumped by 9.1%, accounting for more than half of the increase in inflation, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Overall, energy inflation was up by 20.4% over the year as prices for fuel oil, energy services and electricity climbed. Fuel oil, used in home heating, was up 74.2% over the year.

Experts said the US Federal Reserve - which sets the country's interest rate - will be closely watching to see if energy costs begin to affect other areas of the economy, such as food prices, and drive inflation higher.

At the moment, food inflation remains subdued. It was flat over the month of September, and was 2.5% across the year.

Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, was 2.6%.

Shortly after the latest inflation figure was released, the Social Security Administration announced that Social Security benefits including old age, survivors and disability insurance would rise by a similar amount - 3.6% - in 2027.

The administration said that the 3.6% rise will mean an average retirement benefit increase of $75 a month.
sources.headline: US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices

sources.body:
Economists divided on Fed rate hike as inflation creates uncertainty in run-up to US midterm elections in a tense market.

United States consumer prices jumped in September in the final inflation report before the midterm elections, increasing chances of an interest rate hike later this month.

Annual inflation accelerated to 3.7 percent, up from 3.4 percent in August. On a monthly basis, prices rose by 0.6 percent, according to the Consumer Price Index report released by the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) on Wednesday.

Petrol prices led the surge as tensions between the US and Iran, as well as Russia and Ukraine, weighed on global energy prices. Petrol prices rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for more than half of the CPI monthly increase, according to the BLS. They were up 34.2 percent from the same time a year ago.

“The directionless war in Iran continues to disrupt global supply chains, driving up the prices of food and fuel,” Kyle Moore, chief economist at The Century Foundation, an economic think tank, said in a statement provided to Al Jazeera.

Petrol prices have continued to climb. The average price for a gallon of petrol is $4.33 ($1.14 per litre), compared with $4.31 a month ago, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices. Diesel prices are higher, at $6.29 per gallon (1.66 per litre), compared with $6.23 a month ago.

In a post on X, Patrick DeHaan, head of petroleum analysis for GasBuddy, said, “2026 has now seen more days with average gas prices over $4/gal than any year before: 158 days.”

Shelter costs also jumped 0.4 percent from the previous month, following a 0.3 percent increase in August. Food costs were a bright spot in the report, remaining unchanged overall.

Food away from home, including restaurant meals, rose 0.2 percent, but that increase was offset by a 0.1 percent decline in food-at-home prices, which track grocery costs.

At the grocery store, poultry prices jumped 0.7 percent, fruit and vegetable prices rose 0.5 percent, and juice prices increased 1.1 percent. However, milk prices dropped 2.1 percent and beef prices fell 0.9 percent.

Amid heavy investment in AI infrastructure, prices for computer software and accessories have jumped 28 percent from the same time last year.

“The AI boom is playing a huge part, and we have all read about the hundreds of billions being poured into data centers, AI firms, and models,” Rami Cassis, principal of Parabellum Investment, said in comments provided to Al Jazeera.

The inflation data comes days before the US Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision later this month. Last month, the US central bank raised rates by 25 basis points, bringing the target range to 3.75–4.00 percent, the first hike in three years .

Economists are divided over whether the Fed will raise rates again or hold them steady. According to CME FedWatch, which tracks the likelihood of monetary policy decisions, there is a 52.9 percent chance that rates will remain in the 3.75–4.00 percent range, while a 47.1 percent chance of a quarter of a percentage point hike that would bring them to 4.00–4.25 percent.
sources.headline: US inflation rises before midterm elections, fuelling rate hike fears

stories.headline: Republicans worry that Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan faces a difficult re-election race

sources.body: WASILLA, Alaska — Three weeks out from Election Day, President Donald Trump took a helicopter to a plane to another helicopter to a motorcade to an ice hockey rink in Alaska's Matanuska-Susitna Valley, traversing nearly 4,000 miles over more than eight hours to turn out his base here to help Republicans defend the Senate. But Trump’s trek might not be enough to save Sen. Dan Sullivan, who’s running in a tougher-than-expected race against Democrat Mary Peltola in a state where the president’s approval rating is underwater and independents outnumber both Republicans and Democrats. Alaska strategists and voters who spoke to POLITICO acknowledged that Sullivan faces a difficult path to reelection, despite Trump’s time investment and the outside money pouring in. “Very conservative MAGA voters can’t vote for you harder,” said Scott Kendall, a veteran political strategist who worked on two of Alaska GOP Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s campaigns and was chief of staff to former Alaska Gov. Bill Walker. “Donald Trump’s support in this current climate is both a blessing and a curse.” Even some Trump supporters at the Tuesday night rally admitted the outlook appeared bleak. “I think Alaska’s turning blue,” said Matt Niessink, a 45-year-old general contractor from Wasilla. He said he had voted for Trump three times and planned to support Republicans this year. What did he wish the president would do differently? “I wish he’d shut his mouth sometimes and not be such a pompous ass,” Niessink said. The president was in Wasilla — population 10,556 — because the outlook is darkening for his party in a state he carried by 13 points just two years ago. In a midterm year defined by the cost of gas and groceries, the Last Frontier has been hit particularly hard, with the average price of diesel nearing $7 per gallon. In the Senate race, Peltola is flush with cash and leads Sullivan in most polls. MAGA Inc., the cash-rich Trump-aligned super PAC, is increasingly focusing on Alaska as one in a slate of states that can help Republicans hold the Senate. Enter Trump, who has been spending the cycle’s crucial final weeks holding rallies in red states to juice support among his base, which tends to see depressed turnout in years when he’s not on the ballot. “That was a lot of flying,” the president said at the top of his remarks. “In fact, they were thinking about canceling. They said, ‘Sir, you’re very busy, this is very tough.’” But, Trump continued, he refused to cancel for a state he won three times. Echoing his comments at other red-state rallies, Trump asked the roaring crowd for “one big favor” — to “pretend that I'm on the ballot, because every time I've been on the ballot, we win.” He repeated his promise that Americans will receive $5,000 dividends if Republicans hold both chambers. “What this is about is getting out the vote,” Sullivan told reporters before Trump’s speech. “A rising tide of enthusiasm lifts all the candidates.” Unlike some other Republican candidates in tight races, Sullivan has shied away from distancing himself from the least popular aspects of Trump’s presidency. Sullivan proclaimed on stage at the rally that “the conflict in the Middle East is temporary. The true forever war is the national Democrats’ war against Alaska oil and gas and our jobs.” And although a campaign aide released a statement condemning Trump’s move to import Russian diesel, Sullivan did not join four of his Republican Senate colleagues, including Murkowski, who called on Trump to reverse the decision. Art Hackney, a veteran Republican strategist in Alaska, said that “most of the people who support” Sullivan “think that he should” break more with the president. Hackney, who runs a pro-Sullivan super PAC called “We Stand with Dan,” attributed that choice to loyalty — but suggested the president’s demand of fealty, and treatment of frequent dissenter Murkowski, could also be part of Sullivan’s calculus. “A lot of his longtime supporters and the people who are in the industries that would benefit from that wish he would be more blunt,” Hackney said. “But with what Murkowski has done, if Dan did something considered a disrespectful trigger or something, what do you think would happen? It could well have implications for things that affect Alaska's economy.” Like this content? Consider signing up for POLITICO's Playbook PM newsletter .
sources.headline: ‘I think Alaska’s turning blue’: Republicans fret Sullivan’s path to reelection

stories.headline: Spain’s election campaign turns to pensions as PSOE and PP trade warnings over the system’s future

sources.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/UTT5PBARRZAR5JBXA52PUG5K5M.jpg?auth=03c65e106d6adf76c3ed3ede86575b72865c313752a904cbf8828ce8bb29032f" width="4726" height="3150" alt="Varias personas en el centro de Sevilla, el 5 de octubre."></img><p>Las pensiones son el eterno agujero negro de todas las carreras electorales y esta precampaña del 29-N se incendió este miércoles precisamente por el pulso sobre su futuro. El <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/sanchez-carga-contra-el-pp-por-las-pensiones-si-pp-y-vox-llegan-al-gobierno-firman-la-carta-de-defuncion-del-estado-del-bienestar.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/sanchez-carga-contra-el-pp-por-las-pensiones-si-pp-y-vox-llegan-al-gobierno-firman-la-carta-de-defuncion-del-estado-del-bienestar.html">PSOE y el PP entraron de lleno en la batalla para conseguir el voto de los pensionistas</a>, un espectro de votantes que sigue confiando de forma mayoritaria en los dos grandes partidos. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, está buscando fórmulas legales para poder aprobar una subida de las pensiones justo antes de las elecciones. En paralelo, el partido de Alberto Núñez Feijóo trata de dejar claro que él también siempre apoyará las revalorizaciones con el IPC, en contra de lo que sugirió la portavoz parlamentaria, Ester Muñoz, <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-14/la-portavoz-del-pp-ester-munoz-asegura-que-el-sistema-de-pensiones-va-a-colapsar-y-pide-cambiarlo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-14/la-portavoz-del-pp-ester-munoz-asegura-que-el-sistema-de-pensiones-va-a-colapsar-y-pide-cambiarlo.html">al sostener que el sistema de pensiones “va a petar”</a> y que hay que cambiarlo de forma “valiente”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-15/el-psoe-y-el-pp-encienden-la-batalla-por-el-futuro-de-las-pensiones.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/3O2M732G6NFX7GC4V45HXXZXWY.jpg?auth=b2722452fc8d2745a9e789aabfeb34c95de8be87d28a1a3bc6c52b09506443f5" width="5236" height="2693" alt="La portavoz del PP Ester Muñoz en una sesión de control al Gobierno en el Congreso de los Diputados."></img>
sources.headline: El PSOE y el PP encienden la batalla por el futuro de las pensiones

sources.body:
La portavoz del Gobierno y ministra de Seguridad Social, Elma Saiz, y el ministro de Hacienda, Arcadi España, el pasado martes en Moncloa tras la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Ministros. / José Luis Roca / EPC

El PSOE ha metido de lleno las pensiones en la coctelera de su agenda de campaña, tratando de contraponer modelos con PP y Vox. Al tiempo que en el Gobierno no descartan fórmulas para anticipar su revalorización antes de las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre o anunciar su subida, los ministros socialistas salieron este miércoles en tromba a agitar el miedo a los recortes y hasta a la “privatización” si gobierna la derecha. Lo hicieron después de que el líder de los populares, Alberto Núñez Feijóo , hablase en un mitin de “sacrificios” y la portavoz, Ester Muñoz , avisase durante una entrevista en un pódcast que el sistema actual de pensiones "tal y como está no funciona y va a petar" . Los socialistas aprovecharon el tropezón para asociar “sacrificio” con recortes en las pensiones.

Pedro Sánchez rescató estas palabras de la portavoz del PP durante un mitin en Zaragoza la tarde de este miércoles para acusar a los populares de recortes y de "no decir ni una media verdad". “No es lo mismo un hospital público que uno gestionado por Quirón como no es lo mismo una pensión pública que una gestionada por un gran banco” , contrapuso para comprometerse a “cuatro años más” de revalorización de las pensiones. "No va a haber recortes en los próximos cuatro años, como venimos haciendo durante los últimos ocho años", aseguró abriendo el foco del acceso a la vivienda a la defensa de los servicios públicos y las pensiones.

“Es la primera fase del ciclo de la privatización: el miedo”, replicaba la portavoz del Gobierno y ministra de Seguridad Social, Elma Saiz , para defender que “nuestro sistema público de pensiones es sostenible y es el que quiere la inmensa mayoría de los ciudadanos”. Junto a otros dirigentes socialistas recordaba que “el PP votó en contra de ligar las pensiones al IPC”. “Feijóo hablaba este fin de semana de sacrificios, ahora el PP señala a los pensionistas cómo los primeros en pagarlos”, relacionaba la ministra de Ciencia, Diana Morant, obviando las aclaraciones del PP negando recortes.

El vicepresidente primero y ministro de Economía, Carlos Cuerpo , quien finalmente no irá en las listas como independiente, incidía en esta línea de campaña durante una entrevista en ‘RNE’ a primera hora. “¿Qué quiere hacer cada partido con las pensiones?”, se preguntaba apuntando a mensajes contradictorios dentro del PP. Según deslizó, detrás de esta discusión sobre la sostenibilidad de las pensiones hay un intento porque “lo público deje de tener su espacio y pasemos a un modelo mixto o de capitalización”. Opciones legítimas, dijo, pero que invitó a explicitarlas llamando a un diagnóstico riguroso según el cual el modelo actual garantizaría la actualización conforme al IPC.

El titular de Hacienda, Arcadi España , apuntaba también al sistema mixto de capitalización siguiendo la estela abierta por Vox. Un modelo implantado por la derecha chilena y que ha producido elevadas pérdidas. “Si juntas sacrificio con reforma” del sistema “se me hiela la sangre”, concluía para ver la mano de Vox detrás del programa de los populares. Todo ello a pesar de que Feijóo haya tratado de zanjar el debate garantizado que si gobierna subirá las pensiones actualizándolas conforme a la inflación, a través de “un sistema público y viable”.
sources.headline: El Gobierno agita el miedo a la "privatización" de las pensiones de PP y Vox y estudia subirlas antes del 29N

stories.headline: The United States proposes tariffs on Spanish ships and export sanctions over Spain’s Israel trade embargo

sources.body:
La Comisión Marítima Federal (FMC, por sus siglas en inglés) de Estados Unidos ha propuesto este miércoles aranceles de 200.000 dólares por viaje a todos los buques con bandera española, así como restricciones a la exportación de una serie de productos españoles hacia territorio estadounidense. Es su respuesta al veto del comercio de armas con Israel, que el Gobierno impuso por la guerra en Gaza y los asentamientos ilegales en territorios palestinos ocupados.

La FMC inició una investigación después de que en 2024 se negara el acceso a los puertos españoles a tres buques del Programa de Seguridad Marítima estadounidense, vinculado a la Secretaría de Defensa, alegando que transportaban carga con destino u origen en Israel. En ese momento, ya se aplicaba el embargo de armas , que se amplió más tarde con otras restricciones al comercio israelí.

Tras escuchar a diferentes partes implicadas, incluido el Gobierno de España, el organismo federal ha concluido que esas medidas crean "condiciones desfavorables para el transporte marítimo internacional" y "graves consecuencias" para el desarrollo de las exportaciones estadounidenses.

Por ello, además del arancel de 200.000 dólares por viaje y buque, impone restricciones a las exportaciones de algunos productos españoles de perfumería y cosmética, aceites y grasas, cerámica, artículos de piedra, azúcar y confitería.

Fuentes del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores han aclarado que presentarán alegaciones en el plazo establecido por la FMC, de 60 días desde la publicación en el registro. "Las medidas adoptadas por España en ningún caso son discriminatorias contra Estados Unidos ni contra ningún tercer país, y, por lo tanto, consideramos que cualquier medida sobre esta base carecería de fundamento", han indicado.

Desde el departamento que dirige el ministro José Manuel Albares han garantizado también que defenderán los intereses comerciales y las decisiones soberanas del país, así como el cumplimiento del Derecho de la UE y del Derecho internacional, con el objetivo de evitar las sanciones que, recordamos, no son firmes, sino una propuesta de la FMC.

La FMC ya ha tomado en consideración los argumentos del Gobierno español para realizar su propuesta de sanciones, así como más de 8.000 comentarios en el proceso de participación pública , pero solo en lo referente específicamente al comercio marítimo internacional.

"Muchas de las respuestas a la notificación de diciembre de 2024 se centraron en preocupaciones sobre posibles violaciones de los derechos humanos . Estas cuestiones quedan fuera del alcance de la presente investigación", reza el informe.

Entre esos comentarios, el documento menciona la argumentación de tres congresistas demócratas y la de un antiguo diplomático estadounidense, que defendían la postura española. Por el contrario, se mostraron a favor de la investigación de la FMC desde algunos sindicatos marítimos, que consideraban que las medidas de España "socavan el comercio justo y crean condiciones desfavorables" para los buques estadounidenses.
sources.headline: EE.UU. propone aranceles a los buques espa�oles y sanciones a las exportaciones por el veto comercial a Israel

stories.headline: Spain’s CIS poll puts PSOE 11.8 points ahead of PP, though analysts question the survey’s methodology

sources.body: <p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-se-aferra-a-la-espana-periferica-para-reducir-la-ventaja-de-pp-y-vox.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-se-aferra-a-la-espana-periferica-para-reducir-la-ventaja-de-pp-y-vox.html">El PSOE ganaría las elecciones generales</a> con un 34% del voto en caso de que se celebraran hoy, según el barómetro de octubre del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS), publicado este miércoles. El PSOE crece tres puntos en intención de voto respecto al estudio publicado en septiembre y aumenta su distancia sobre el PP hasta los 11,8 puntos. El instituto dirigido por José Félix Tezanos deja a los populares en segunda posición con el 22,2% de los sufragios, 3,3 puntos menos que en septiembre. La tercera fuerza del Parlamento en intención de voto es el partido de Santiago Abascal, que suma medio punto respecto a septiembre y obtiene el 17,1% del voto. Las formaciones <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-13/los-partidos-del-frente-amplio-acuerdan-que-emilio-delgado-sea-numero-uno-por-madrid.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-13/los-partidos-del-frente-amplio-acuerdan-que-emilio-delgado-sea-numero-uno-por-madrid.html">de Sumar/Frente Amplio</a> reciben un 6,1% de los apoyos y Podemos pierde seis décimas, quedándose en el 3,1%. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-aumenta-la-distancia-sobre-el-pp-hasta-los-118-puntos-tras-la-convocatoria-electoral-segun-el-cis.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El PSOE aumenta la distancia sobre el PP hasta los 11,8 puntos tras la convocatoria electoral, según el CIS

sources.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/OEQOOHBQZNFBBJRLV7JGZCKFO4.jpg?auth=14067dcccec9e678fed24defc650a9c30fd7e8bc0a9d77358a5265000d4c0c1e" width="6000" height="3375" alt="José Félix Tezanos, presidente del CIS, en su comparecencia en el Senado en diciembre del año pasado. "></img><p>El <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-aumenta-la-distancia-sobre-el-pp-hasta-los-118-puntos-tras-la-convocatoria-electoral-segun-el-cis.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-aumenta-la-distancia-sobre-el-pp-hasta-los-118-puntos-tras-la-convocatoria-electoral-segun-el-cis.html">avance del último barómetro del CIS</a> ha reavivado la polémica por las <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-10-14/hay-que-ignorar-las-estimaciones-de-voto-del-cis.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-10-14/hay-que-ignorar-las-estimaciones-de-voto-del-cis.html">sobreestimaciones </a>de los apoyos del PSOE en los que ha incurrido el Centro en Investigaciones Sociológicas en más de una ocasión. La encuesta pública, con una muestra de gran tamaño (5.000 entrevistas) sitúa a los socialistas no solo a la cabeza en estimación de voto, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-aumenta-la-distancia-sobre-el-pp-hasta-los-118-puntos-tras-la-convocatoria-electoral-segun-el-cis.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-aumenta-la-distancia-sobre-el-pp-hasta-los-118-puntos-tras-la-convocatoria-electoral-segun-el-cis.html">sino casi 12 puntos por delante del PP</a>. Esos porcentajes distan mucho del promedio de sondeos privados. Ese mismo avance facilitado por el CIS muestra que en la escala de auto-ubicación ideológica, siendo el 1 la extrema izquierda y 10 la extrema derecha, el 18,9% se sitúa a sí mismo en el 1, casi tanto (22%) como los que se ubican en el 5, es decir, el centro. Los expertos consultados por este diario coinciden en señalar que no recuerdan una diferencia tan grande entre lo que dice el Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas y el resto de encuestas. También apuntan a un mismo fallo: la sobrerrepresentación de votantes del PSOE en esa muestra de la población que debe ser lo más parecida posible al conjunto. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-15/por-que-tantos-sociologos-no-se-creen-la-encuesta-del-cis-el-sesgo-en-la-muestra-contamina-las-encuestas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Por qué tantos sociólogos no se creen la encuesta del CIS: el sesgo en la muestra contamina las encuestas

stories.headline: Spain’s left seeks a last-minute unified election ticket as the coalition-registration deadline nears

sources.body:
Mientras arrancan las primarias en Podemos, donde Irene Montero aspira a convertirse en el referente de la formación para las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, continúan las negociaciones entre los partidos de izquierdas, que sobre la bocina intentan sellar una candidatura de unidad. El plazo para presentar coaliciones concluye el próximo viernes, pero no termina de materializarse el pacto entre los morados y Frente Amplio , formación que aglutina a Izquierda Unida, Movimiento Sumar, los Comunes y Más Madrid.

Este miércoles, la exalcaldesa de Barcelona, Ada Colau , que fue designada como candidata de esa formación a la presidencia del Gobierno, se ha mostrado dispuesta a ceder ese liderazgo "si hay otra persona que genera más consenso que mi candidatura".

En una entrevista en el programa La hora de la 1 de TVE, ha ido incluso más allá, señalando que " si el problema es el nombre de la formación, se cambia ". "Todo se puede discutir", ha dicho antes de pedir "acuerdos valientes". Habiendo "una enorme coincidencia" a nivel programático, ha advertido, " nadie entendería que no nos pusiésemos de acuerdo ": "No se nos perdonaría que por temas de marcas no se hiciera candidatura unitaria". Por eso se ha mostrado "abierta a discutir nombres, candidaturas, listas".

En la misma línea, el coordinador federal de Izquierda Unida, Antonio Maíllo , ha destacado la "voluntad inequívoca" de construir una gran alianza. Desde una rueda de prensa celebrada en el parlamento andaluz, Maíllo ha descrito la oferta lanzada por Colau como "la desnudez y honestidad en cuanto a la voluntad inequívoca de construir una alianza amplia ".

"Las cartas están sobre la mesa", ha continuado Maíllo, que ha asegurado que "todo es más fácil de lo que parece": "Nosotros estamos abiertos a una alianza amplia", ha señalado, diciendo que el resto de formaciones "que decidan lo que consideren y asuman la necesidad de responsabilidad del momento histórico que vivimos".

“ Juntarse para crecer. Crecer para ganar. Ganar para vivir. Este sábado nos vemos en el Parque Lineal del Manzanares. Es la hora del Frente Amplio. Apoya en https://t.co/qMSHdCtDcj https://t.co/ategGpdhf6 “

Fuentes de Frente Amplio, que ha dado a conocer su imagen y su logo, y convocado un gran acto el próximo sábado en Madrid para presentar su proyecto, han asegurado que Colau ha manifestado la voluntad de esa formación de "alcanzar acuerdos con todas las fuerzas políticas". También que la exalcaldesa de Barcelona "se toma muy en serio la unidad".

"Esa unidad, abierta y generosa, forma parte del ADN del Frente Amplio desde su origen, un proyecto que lleva año y medio cocinándose a fuego lento", dicen las mismas fuentes, que presentan como prioridades de su proyecto "la defensa del derecho a la vivienda y responder a lo que se exige en las plazas y las calles".

También el ministro de Cultura y miembro de la dirección de Comúns, Ernest Urtasun, ha pedido "unidad" y el voto de los ciudadanos para que den "la mayor fuerza posible" a su partido y a Frente Amplio. El objetivo, llevar "con toda la fuerza posible" al Gobierno de Coalición y el Congreso de los Diputados políticas como las incluidas en los decretos de vivienda que ha de convalidar la Diputación Permanente.
sources.headline: La izquierda busca in extremis una alianza y Podemos celebra primarias cerca de acabar el plazo para registrar coaliciones

stories.headline: Barcelona moves to raise property tax on tourist apartments by up to 150%

sources.body: No fa ni 10 dies que es va obrir la possibilitat perquè Barcelona pugui apujar al màxim l’impost sobre els béns immobles ( IBI ) als pisos turístics de la ciutat, però el govern de Jaume Collboni s’ha apressat per poder-ho fer realitat. De fet, l’executiu ja va dur la carpeta a una Comissió d’Economia i Hisenda extraordinària i, ara, ha convocat un plenari també extraordinari per seguir avançant en la qüestió. Si no hi ha cap gir de guió inesperat, el triumvirat PSC-BComú-ERC permetrà que el Ple doni la seva primera llum verda a aquesta modificació de les ordenances fiscals per encarir fins a un 150 % l’IBI als propietaris dels habitatges d’ús turístic (HUT). Aquest encariment es farà en funció del nombre de pisos que tingui cada propietari. Per a qui en tingui un, el recàrrec de l’IBI serà del 50 % . Per a qui en tingui dos, tres o quatre, el recàrrec de l’IBI serà del 100 % . Per a qui en tingui més de quatre, el recàrrec serà del 150 % . També et pot interessar L’Ajuntament vol eliminar tots els pisos turístics de Barcelona el novembre del 2028 Josep Bassas Sergio Segura Sílvia Gutiérrez 2 minuts de lectura Quants pisos turístics hi ha a Barcelona? Aquest encariment progressiu permetrà a l’Ajuntament incidir específicament en els propietaris que acumulin més pisos turístics sota un mateix titular. De fet, les 10.627 llicències d’HUT de Barcelona es reparteixen així: 3.274 pisos turístics estan en mans de titulars que només en tenen un. 1.276 pisos turístics estan en mans de titulars que en tenen dos, tres o quatre a nom seu. 6.077 pisos turístics estan en mans de titulars que en tenen més de quatre a nom seu. Un cop el Plenari doni la primera llum verda a aquesta modificació de les ordenances fiscals, l’expedient quedarà en exposició pública perquè s’hi puguin fer al·legacions, mentre que l’aprovació definitiva serà a finals d’any. L’encariment de l’IBI és una estratègia més per declarar la guerra als pisos turístics, abans que Barcelona els pugui eliminar definitivament el 2028 . També et pot interessar Pedro Sánchez troba una via alternativa per aprovar els decrets d’habitatge tombats pel Congrés Marina Segura i Vidal 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: Un ple extraordinari donarà llum verda a l’IBI més alt de la història per als pisos turístics

stories.headline: Catalonia faces a possible weekend of heavy rain and rough seas as a DANA approaches

sources.body:
Dana sobre Catalunya en noviembre de 2024.

La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) prevé un cambio significativo del tiempo durante el próximo fin de semana, con un aumento de la inestabilidad que afectará especialmente a Baleares y a la vertiente mediterránea peninsular. El episodio dejará precipitaciones intensas y persistentes, junto a un acusado descenso generalizado de las temperaturas. La lluvia sucederá a unos días de sol con temperaturas impropias de estos días del año.

Según una nota informativa de la Aemet difundida este miércoles, la elongación de una vaguada sobre la Península y el probable aislamiento de una dana al norte favorecerán la formación de chubascos y tormentas. Al mismo tiempo, las altas presiones situadas en el entorno de las Islas Británicas y el mar del Norte facilitarán la entrada de una masa de aire más frío, lo que permitirá que las temperaturas tiendan a normalizarse.

La Aemet señala que el episodio podría comenzar el sábado 17 de octubre, cuando un sistema frontal afectará al Cantábrico y se desarrollarán chubascos y tormentas en zonas del interior peninsular. Durante la segunda mitad del día, las precipitaciones tenderían a intensificarse y extenderse hacia Baleares y la fachada mediterránea, mientras que las temperaturas descenderán de forma generalizada y de manera notable en el cuadrante noroeste.

El domingo 18, el escenario considerado más probable por la Aemet sitúa las precipitaciones más importantes en los litorales y prelitorales mediterráneos y en Baleares. Las lluvias podrían ser intensas y persistentes, con acumulaciones relevantes a lo largo del episodio, aunque también se esperan chubascos y tormentas en otros puntos del interior. Las temperaturas volverán a bajar en buena parte de la Península, especialmente en la mitad oriental.

La Aemet advierte, no obstante, de que persiste una elevada incertidumbre sobre la posición definitiva de la dana y de la vaguada, así como sobre los flujos de viento en superficie, factores que determinarán la distribución y la intensidad de las precipitaciones. Por ello, el organismo recomienda seguir las actualizaciones de los pronósticos durante los próximos días para concretar las zonas que podrían resultar más afectadas.
sources.headline: La Aemet alerta de una dana y de un desplome de las temperaturas para el fin de semana

stories.headline: Only half of Catalan municipalities required to have flood-emergency plans have current ones

sources.body:
Aquest mes d'octubre hem patit diversos episodis de pluges intenses que han causat inundacions arreu del país. Han provocat importants danys materials en algunes localitats i diverses víctimes mortals .

Els experts vaticinen que, amb la crisi climàtica , aquests fenòmens extrems seran cada cop més freqüents , i per això cal que la ciutadania i les administracions estiguem preparats.

Una de les eines que tenen els ajuntaments per fer-hi front són els plans d'emergència per inundacions , uns documents que han d'estar homologats per Protecció Civil .

Els plans municipals d'actuació per risc d'inundacions "pretenen evitar les improvisacions", segons explica a 3CatInfo Álvaro González , cap del Servei de Plans i Recursos de Protecció Civil.

Aquests documents estableixen l'estructura de resposta, l'operativa i els procediments necessaris per gestionar qualsevol emergència associada a les inundacions amb la finalitat de minimitzar el risc i garantir la seguretat de les persones i la protecció dels béns, les infraestructures i el medi ambient.

Els elaboren els ajuntaments , "ja que són els millors coneixedors del territori", segons González, i s'han d'anar actualitzant periòdicament .

Sant Pere de Ribes acaba de rebre l'homologació del seu pla. L'alcaldessa, Ana Herrera , explica que "està molt ben definit" i que detalla quines són les persones responsables que han d'actuar en cas d'una alerta, quins comunicats s'han de fer a la població o quines actuacions cal fer per controlar l'emergència, com, per exemple, tancar les carreteres que travessen rieres i prohibir l'estacionament preventivament, entre d'altres.

La normativa de Protecció Civil obliga 655 municipis a tenir un pla municipal d'actuació per risc d'inundacions, ja que presenten un risc alt o molt alt . La resta de localitats presenten un risc baix o moderat i, per tant, se'ls recomana tenir-ne, però no és obligatori que ho facin.

El 50,2% dels municipis obligats (329) ja tenen un pla aprovat i homologat per part de Protecció Civil. Els darrers a incorporar-se a aquesta llista han estat Sant Pere de Ribes, Sentmenat, l'Ametlla del Vallès, Sant Hilari Sacalm i Premià de Dalt, entre d'altres.

En canvi, 223 municipis ( 34% ) en tenen però pendent de revisió ; és a dir, el tenen caducat. Alguns pobles i ciutats, des de fa pocs mesos; d'altres, des de fa vint anys, com és el cas de Martorell, l'Escala i Pineda de Mar.

Finalment, 103 municipis no n'han tingut mai , una xifra que equival al 15,7% . Hi ha casos especialment significatius, com Badalona, quarta ciutat del país en nombre d'habitants, o Rubí, municipi recordat per la tràgica rierada del 1962.
sources.headline: Només el 50% de municipis obligats a tenir un pla d'emergència per inundacions el té vigent: consulta el mapa

stories.headline: The Manyanet school congregation sues the parents of two students who died by suicide

sources.body: La congregació titular de les escoles Manyanet ha demandat per vulneració de l’honor les famílies de dos alumnes de centres de Barcelona que es van suïcidar el 2019 i el 2021. Els demandats són els pares de la Kira , que era alumna a Sant Andreu, i de l’ Òscar , que es va treure la vida als 21 anys i que havia estudiat abans al centre de les Corts. La institució considera que els pares han fet contra ells “acusacions molt greus” a través de les xarxes i d’entrevistes. Els demanen 70.000 euros , segons ha avançat 3Cat. Fonts de la congregació Fills de la Sagrada Família han explicat a betevé que el detonant de la demanda està relacionat amb el cas de l’Òscar. Fa anys que la família sospita que el noi podria haver patit abusos sexuals per part d’un capellà quan encara era alumne del centre i que l’entitat no va fer prou per impedir-ho. És una acusació, segons aquestes fonts, “sense proves”, que hauria estat “induïda” per l’altre pare demandat, el de la Kira, i amb mitjans de l’ associació Trencats , contra la qual també s’interposa la demanda. “Ens estem defensant”, asseguren des de la congregació. “La demanda no té fonament”, segons l’advocada Per a l’advocada que representa l’associació i les famílies, Noelia Rebón, els pares “no s’estan inventant res”. El capellà Joaquim Calvet va ser condemnat el 2023 per tinença de pornografia infantil després que el denunciés un informàtic de l’escola Manyanet de Sant Andreu, on també va ser docent. “Els pares no són responsables de la reputació de les escoles”, diu Rebón, que creu que la demanda “busca silenciar-los”. Enfrontaments judicials oberts No és l’únic litigi obert entre les dues parts. El centre Pare Manyanet ja es va querellar fa dos anys contra els pares de la Kira per injúries i calúmnies. Tot i que la causa es va arxivar inicialment, l’abril d’aquest any la congregació va presentar un recurs que ha estat admès a tràmit. Al gener se celebrarà el judici sobre la responsabilitat civil de l’escola per la suposada inacció davant de l’assetjament patit per la Kira. També et pot interessar L’audiència prèvia del judici pel cas de la Kira confronta família i escola Abigail Armengol 2 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: La congregació de les escoles Manyanet demanda els pares de dos alumnes que es van suïcidar

sources.body:
La congregació Fills de la Sagrada Família, titular de les escoles Pare Manyanet , ha demandat els pares de dos alumnes de centres de Barcelona que es van suïcidar: la Kira , el 2021, i l'Òscar , el 2019. Segons ha pogut saber 3CatInfo , els demana 70.000 euros per haver vulnerat l'honor de la institució.

Els pares de la Kira, que es va suïcidar amb quinze anys, creuen que l'escola Pare Manyanet de Sant Andreu no va protegir la seva filla de l'assetjament escolar que patia.

Els de l'Òscar, que es va treure la vida als 21 anys, quan ja no era alumne del centre de les Corts, sospiten que el seu fill podria haver patit abusos sexuals per part d'un professor de l'escola.

És, precisament, el capellà Joaquim Calvet , a qui anys després van condemnar perquè li van trobar més de 35.000 arxius de vídeos d'explotació sexual infantil al seu ordinador i a qui també van jutjar per, presumptament, haver abusat d'un alumne de vuit anys amb discapacitat.

Els pares de la Kira i l'Òscar han manifestat públicament , en entrevistes i vídeos a mitjans de comunicació, que sospiten que l'escola Pare Manyanet no va protegir els seus fills, i això els ha costat una demanda . L'entitat titular de l'escola els demana 70.000 euros per haver vulnerat el seu honor i la seva imatge.

L'advocada especialista en la protecció de la infància Noelia Rebón , que exerceix la representació dels pares, creu que la demanda no té fonament:

Del que s'hauria de preocupar aquesta congregació és de vigilar perquè les persones que treballen allà i tenen contacte amb nens no tinguin segons quines conductes que poden ser delictives.

Consultades per 3CatInfo, fonts de la institució asseguren que amb la demanda busquen " protegir-se d'acusacions greus sense cap prova ni fonament".

Confirmen que l'han presentada "després d'una acumulació reiterada i acreditada de múltiples missatges als mitjans digitals per part dels acusats, que poden ser constitutius d'una presumpta infracció contra el dret a l'honor i a la pròpia imatge".

Entre aquests missatges que cita la demanda hi ha, per exemple, un vídeo que el pare de l'Òscar va penjar al seu Instagram, en què explicava que el sacerdot Joaquim Calvet viu en una residència molt propera a l'escola i que "des de la terrassa pot escollir les seves víctimes, si vol".

Per Rebón, això no és objecte de demanda "perquè el que està dient és que un senyor que té material pedòfil, i que està acusat d'haver agredit un nen amb discapacitat, des de la terrassa té accés a veure els nens que són al pati".

Pel que fa als pares de la Kira , fa dos anys, l'escola Pare Manyanet de Sant Andreu ja es va querellar contra ells per injúries i calúmnies. Una querella que es va arxivar l'abril del 2026. La institució hi va presentar un recurs d'apel·lació i la justícia va determinar que calia practicar diligències.

L'advocada creu que la demanda és "una manera d'intentar silenciar " aquests pares, que volen esbrinar què va portar els seus fills al suïcidi.

"A mitjans de gener, es celebrarà el judici sobre la responsabilitat civil del Pare Manyanet en el cas de la Kira", explica. Per això, Rebón creu que "no és casual" que la demanda arribi, precisament, en aquest moment, quan falten pocs mesos per aquest judici.
sources.headline: La congregació de l'escola Pare Manyanet demanda els pares de dos alumnes que es van suïcidar
